chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Uthman ibn Sa'id, from Abu al-Mahamil, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The human being is more rightful over (the distribution of) his wealth for as long as the soul is in his body.

key_terms.أحق: More rightful, having greater entitlement — a comparative form indicating priority of right
key_terms.الإنسان: The human being — used universally, encompassing both men and women
key_terms.البدن: The body — physical body as the vessel of the soul during life
key_terms.الروح: The soul/spirit — its departure marks the legal moment of death
key_terms.المال: Wealth, property, assets — all forms of property and financial resources

ai.seo_question: Does a person have full right over their wealth while alive according to Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) affirms the principle that a living person retains full legal authority over their wealth. This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence regarding deathbed bequests (wasiyya) and charitable donations: one's dispositions made while alive and mentally competent are legally binding and cannot be overridden by potential heirs. The phrase 'as long as the soul is in the body' demarcates the moment of death as the legal boundary after which inheritance rules apply.
